subject: LodeStar RFI: KMS architecture, rotation cadence, and TLS handshake details
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lodestar-analytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: security@lodestar-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Keys & TLS for LodeStar evaluation

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. We're compiling a final security appendix for our platform evaluation and need a short set of clear answers and evidence about Redwood's key management and TLS posture so we can present to our compliance committee next week. Specific asks below — please treat this as a single consolidated RFI item and attach any diagrams or artifacts you can share.

1) KMS model: describe whether keys are tenant-isolated, host-managed, or customer BYOK options; list supported HSM vendors and whether Redwood supports customer-managed HSMs (on-prem / cloud).

2) Key rotation policy: recommended rotation cadence for KEK/CEK, supported automated rotation workflows, crypto-agility (algorithm rollover), emergency key zeroization procedure.

3) TLS & handshake: minimum TLS versions supported, mutual TLS for control-plane, client certificate validation, and any specific cipher restrictions for inter-service traffic and user-facing endpoints.

4) Evidence: a diagram of the KMS architecture, a sample rotation schedule matrix, and any HSM attestation/cert bundles you can share (audit-friendly artifacts).

Target: consolidated response + artifacts by EOD 20 May if possible (we know it's tight). If you need a short call, we can make time tomorrow morning.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Mercer
Security Architect, LodeStar Analytics
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@lodestar-analytics.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Keys & TLS for LodeStar evaluation

Alex —

Thanks for the clear checklist. We can consolidate this and attach the artifacts you requested. High-level answers below and I attached the architecture diagram and rotation matrix for the committee. We also included an HSM certificate bundle to demonstrate vendor attestation.

Summary (short):
- KMS model: Redwood supports hosted tenant-isolated keys by default, Dedicated customers may use a dedicated KMS instance backed by customer-owned HSMs; BYOK is supported via KMIP or PKCS#11 (import/wrap options). Supported HSMs: Thales Luna, AWS CloudHSM, and Entrust nShield (customer-managed HSMs can be integrated via our private deployment).
- Rotation: Recommended KEK rotation is 180 days for customer-managed KEKs, 90 days for Redwood-managed KEKs by default; CEKs are rotated per deployment/major-version or on policy-trigger (recommended 30–90 days depending on workload). Automated rotation workflows are available (configurable windows, staged rollouts, and live rollback). Emergency zeroization: HSM-level zeroize + control-plane revocation + rekey playbook (documented).
- TLS: We require TLS 1.2 minimum and support TLS 1.3 for all customer-facing endpoints. Control-plane mutual TLS (mTLS) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments; internal service-to-service traffic uses mTLS with short-lived certs via our internal CA. We restrict ciphers to AEAD suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) and disallow legacy RSA-only key exchanges.

Attachments included: lodestar_kms_arch_diagram.pdf, rotation_schedule_matrix.xlsx, redwood_kms_hsm_cert_bundles.zip

If it's helpful, we can run a short 30-minute technical walkthrough tomorrow where Marcus or Irene can step through the diagram and answer questions about the BYOK import flow and attestation artifacts.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Solutions Engineer — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: LodeStar RFI — draft clarifications and ask allocations

Team,

Quick internal note to scope the artifacts and confirm owners before Hannah sends the final package:
- I will extract the HSM attestation bundles and redact any vendor internal IDs; I'll also prepare the KMIP import sample request (JSON example) and a short checklist for customer BYOK onboarding. (Irene)
- Marcus, can you validate the rotation cadence language? I suggest we present two profiles: "Conservative" (KEK 180d / CEK 90d) and "High-rotation" (KEK 90d / CEK 30d) and call out performance/cost tradeoffs. (Marcus)
- Jordan, please prepare a 10-slide deck for the 30-minute walkthrough focusing on TLS choices and mTLS controls, with a short slide showing our internal CA rotation cadence and cert lifetime (we use 7 days for ephemeral service certs and 30 days for control-plane certs).

Also note a couple of clarifications we should surface to the customer explicitly:
- BYOK import: Redwood supports both import-of-wrapped-keys (customer wraps CEKs with a KEK) and KMIP direct provisioning. For cloud HSMs we recommend using CloudHSM-backed KEKs with tenant isolation in Dedicated/private deployments.
- Emergency zeroization: include HSM serial-trigger instructions and the audit log excerpt that demonstrates an example zeroize event (we'll redact timestamps).

I'll assemble the final zip and hand it to Hannah for delivery. Timeline: Hannah sends final by 17:00 PT today.

Irene
Senior Security Engineer, RedTeam — Redwood Inference

Hannah —

Received, thank you for the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple quick follow-ups from the committee after a quick read:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood's hosted tenant-isolated keys provide per-tenant KEK separation at rest (i.e., unique master KEK per tenant) or whether a shared KEK is used with tenant wrapping?
- For BYOK via KMIP, can you provide the sample KMIP server endpoint snippet and whether your import supports asynchronous key activation (we prefer an activation window that allows pre-provisioning without immediate use).
- For the HSM attestation bundle, could you include the vendor-signed firmware hash and FIPS/CC references if available (if redaction is needed, only redact serials not certs).

We'd like to schedule the 30-minute walkthrough Tuesday 25 May at 10:00 AM PT if that works for your team. Please confirm who will join (we prefer someone who can speak to the actual key import flow).

If you can answer the three bulleted clarifications in a short follow-up email and confirm the walkthrough, that should close the RFI for our committee review.

Regards,
Alex
On Thu, 20 May 2027 at 11:45 AM hannah_schmitt@redwood.com wrote:
> Alex —
>
> Quick answers to the follow-ups you listed:
> - Tenant KEK separation: hosted tenant-isolated keys are implemented with a unique KEK per tenant; we do not use a shared KEK for tenant data encryption. For Dedicated/private deployments customers can bring their own KEK into an HSM boundary.
> - KMIP import: attached KMIP snippet in the drive link and our import supports staging/pre-activation windows (you can provision keys with a scheduled activation timestamp).
> - HSM attestation: we'll provide vendor-signed firmware hash info where allowed; we'll keep serial numbers redacted per vendor policy but will include FIPS/CC references.
>
> Walkthrough: confirmed for Tue 25 May 10:00 AM PT. I'll loop in Marcus and Irene as subject matter experts.
>
> Best,
> Hannah
